cat >> docs/usage.rst <<'EOF'

Immutable version manipulation
------------------------------

``VersionInfo`` exposes read-only components and can be iterated in the order
major, minor, patch, prerelease, build. Numeric components are converted to
integers and non-None prerelease and build values to strings::

    >>> version = semver.VersionInfo(1, 2, 3, 'rc.1')
    >>> tuple(version)
    (1, 2, 3, 'rc.1', None)
    >>> str(version.bump_patch())
    '1.2.4'
    >>> str(version.replace(minor=4, prerelease=None))
    '1.4.3'
    >>> semver.replace('1.2.3+build.1', patch=4)
    '1.2.4+build.1'

The ``bump_major``, ``bump_minor``, ``bump_patch``, ``bump_prerelease`` and
``bump_build`` methods return new instances, leaving the original unchanged.
Tuple comparisons use semantic version precedence, just like comparisons with
other ``VersionInfo`` objects; build metadata does not affect precedence.

Command-line interface
----------------------

Run ``python -m semver`` (or the ``pysemver`` launcher) with one of these commands::

    pysemver compare 1.2.3 2.0.0
    pysemver bump patch 1.2.3
    pysemver check 1.2.3

``compare`` prints -1, 0, or 1. ``bump`` accepts major, minor, patch, prerelease,
or build and prints the updated version. ``check`` produces no output for a
valid version. Invalid versions cause a nonzero exit status and an error on
standard error. Use ``--help`` to see the command syntax.
EOF
cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{
  "R1": 1.0,
  "R2": 1.0,
  "R3": 0.98,
  "R4": 0.99,
  "R5": 0.99,
  "R6": 0.9,
  "R7": 0.99
}
